I don't have a shell tool available in this session to run the test suite, but the fix is minimal and self-contained. Summary of changes:

- `src/domain/tasks.ts`: in `createTasks`, before resolving a `depends_on` ref through `tempIdToTaskId`, check if it equals the spec's own `temp_id` and throw `Task with temp_id "X" cannot depend on itself` — a clear, actionable error instead of the opaque one from `addDependency`.
- `dependencies.ts`'s `addDependency` self-dependency check is untouched, so direct real-id self-deps (e.g. `add_dependency(taskId, taskId)`) still throw `"A task cannot depend on itself"` exactly as before.
- Added a test in `tests/create-tasks.test.ts` covering the self-referencing `temp_id` case.

resultText:
Good, that test calls `addDependency` directly and is untouched by this change — `dependencies.ts` is unmodified.

## Root cause

In `createTasks` (`src/domain/tasks.ts`), when a spec's `depends_on` entry equals its own `temp_id`, `tempIdToTaskId.get(ref)` resolves to the task's own freshly-created real id, so `addDependency(db, ownTaskId, ownTaskId)` was called — hitting the generic, opaque `"A task cannot depend on itself"` check in `dependencies.ts` with no mention of which spec/temp_id caused it.

## Fix

Added a check in the dependency-wiring loop of `createTasks` that detects `ref === spec.temp_id` *before* resolving through the temp_id map, throwing `Task with temp_id "<temp_id>" cannot depend on itself`. This only intercepts the temp_id self-reference case; real task ids (and `addDependency`'s own self-dep/cycle checks) are untouched, so a direct self-dependency on an existing task still fails with the original `"A task cannot depend on itself"` error exactly as before.

Also added a regression test in `tests/create-tasks.test.ts` covering the new clear error, and confirmed rollback (no tasks persisted) matches the pattern used by the other batch-failure tests.
